name: Korean nationalism
summary: Korean nationalism centres on the minjok, an ethnic nation of shared blood, culture and history traced to the legendary founder Dangun. It arose as resistance to Japanese colonial rule and great-power domination, and it aims at a sovereign, ideally reunified, Korean nation. Its strands include ethnic minjok nationalism (more common on the anti-imperialist left and in the democracy movement) and state nationalism tied to the ROK or DPRK.
scope: The mainstream modern minjok nationalism of Korea from the early 20th-century historiography of Shin Chae-ho and the independence movement through South Korean ethnic and state nationalism. It treats Shin's anarchist turn, the North Korean Juche fusion of ethnicity and one-party rule, and the recent decline of reunification sentiment as variants rather than the core. Economic and social questions are mostly outside the ideology and are answered with low confidence.

public-ownership.rationale: No settled view: the state-nationalist right favored state-directed industry while the minjok left leaned toward public control, so adherents split.

unions-good.rationale: The democracy movement of the 1980s was cast as ethnic nationalism against authoritarian rule and the declaration puts the masses at the center, so labor is mildly welcomed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Solidarity of the whole minjok makes cutting welfare for fellow nationals uncongenial, though the ideology has no welfare program.

surveillance-ok.rationale: State nationalism backed security-state measures against the North, while ethnic nationalism opposed authoritarian regimes, so adherents split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Shin warns ethnic nationalism fused with racism is dangerous, but nationalism itself offers no speech doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: State nationalism served strongmen like Rhee and Park, while ethnic nationalism was also the language of anti-authoritarian movements.

state-harmful.rationale: Korean nationalism aims at a sovereign nation-state and even at reunifying two states, so the idea that the state is unnecessary is rejected.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Modern Korean nationalism took shape under Japanese rule precisely to protect Korean culture, history and identity.

gradual-change.rationale: Anti-colonial nationalism was a revolutionary and insurgent project that rejected waiting, though mainstream post-war nationalism is institutional.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ethnic-descent nationhood favors limiting newcomers, though economic need and a multiethnic reality complicate it.

nation-first.rationale: Putting the minjok and its sovereignty first is the core of the ideology, though Korean nationalism is mainly defensive rather than isolationist.

open-borders.rationale: A nation defined by shared blood makes open borders contrary to the ideology, per Shin's account of descent-based citizenship.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No nationalist doctrine; energy self-sufficiency and security concerns pull both ways.

revolution-justified.rationale: Shin's declaration calls violence the weapon of revolution against foreign rule; mainstream nationalism accepts armed resistance to colonialism but also nonviolent protest.

central-planning.rationale: Not a nationalist position; developmentalist state nationalism used state direction within a market economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State nationalism under Park Chung-hee tied national strength to state-led industrialization.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a nationalist aim; Shin's anarchism is outside the mainstream.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State nationalism favored state-coordinated economy but ethnic nationalism has no such doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: South Korean nationalism is democratic in its mainstream, though North Korea's Juche state fuses ethnicity with one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Shin's declaration targets privileged classes and 'servile' thought, and modern Korean nationalism is republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Younger South Koreans draw national pride from democratic institutions and 1980s nationalism opposed authoritarianism, but state nationalism accommodated dictators.

natural-rulers.rationale: Shin explicitly condemns privileged classes and the idea that heroes or elites should lead; the masses make the revolution.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed resistance to colonial rule is honored, but the 1919 independence movement was largely nonviolent.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not a feature of Korean nationalism, which is ethnic and secular in form.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic nationalism rests on the belief that Koreans are a nation of shared blood and ancestry, and Shin treats the minjok as the foundation of history.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Shin made the minjok and its struggle against others, not class, the center of history; mainstream nationalism puts nation above class.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-Japanese sentiment centers on colonial cruelty, comfort women and compensation grievances, so Korean nationalists press the principle strongly.

civilizational-union.rationale: Shin rejected subordination to Chinese or Japanese influence; a pan-civilizational union is not a Korean nationalist aim.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Shin notes ethnic nationalism subordinated individual rights to the collective.

restore-past-order.rationale: Shin rejects privileged class and servile traditions; the goal is national restoration, not old social order.

direct-action.rationale: Shin's declaration advocates direct revolution; mainstream nationalists use elections and diplomacy, so split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Shin holds destruction and construction are inseparable, but the mainstream has no view.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Shin condemns economic exploitation, but mainstream nationalism takes no stand on profit theory.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a nationalist doctrine; anti-imperialism targets great powers not capitalism as such.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Shin documents ethnic nationalism placing the collective above individual rights.

conscription.rationale: South Korean national defense relies on conscription, and the 2011 enlistment oath change shows military service is tied to national identity.

positive-liberty.rationale: The ideology's freedom concern is national independence, not material capability, so it is neutral here.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nationalists did criticize colonial scholarship, but no doctrine on media and universities' power exists.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Shin notes Koreans did not clearly distinguish ethnicity from race, but this audit finds no doctrine on genetic ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a feature of Korean nationalism.

total-state.rationale: State nationalism drew on Showa statism but total control of life is not a mainstream nationalist demand.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Shin's claims about lost northern lands are historiographic and mainstream nationalism is not expansionist.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to the declaration's opposition to privilege and exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalist historiography treats Japanese colonial history as politically motivated, but the ideology has no epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: Nationalism speaks of one people, but has no theory of a rationally determined common good; neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Descent-based citizenship lets overseas Koreans regain citizenship more easily than migrants.

school-vouchers.rationale: School funding mechanisms are unrelated to the ideology; neutral.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of Korean nationalism; adherents differ by party.

economic-freedom.rationale: The ideology does not tie political freedom to economic freedom either way.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial independence and resistance to foreign domination is the founding purpose of Korean nationalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not a nationalist issue; adherents split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving the nation's culture and history is central, so sacrificing heritage institutions is rejected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Shin warns ethnic nationalism fused with racism is dangerous; segregation law is not a Korean nationalist demand.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not a nationalist question.

national-mission.rationale: Korean nationalism is defensive and identity-preserving, not a missionary export of its system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hostility to privileged classes is in Shin, yet mainstream nationalism lends no common view.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Pure-blood ideology supports it traditionally, while Korea's multiethnic society and 2011 oath change show rejection, so adherents split.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Shin warns racist fusion is dangerous and tolerance has lagged, so abstract equal worth is agreed but ethnic hierarchy of membership persists.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist strategy is outside Korean nationalism's concerns.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not a Korean nationalist topic; neutral.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Shin accepts violence against foreign rule; mainstream nationalists accept resisting colonial force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Shin sees history as struggle of peoples, but the mainstream has no doctrine.

vanguard-party.rationale: The declaration says the masses themselves lead the revolution, not a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The ideology gives no priority rule for the poor; adherents split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are unrelated to Korean nationalist thought.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not a nationalist issue; adherents split by left and right.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic homogeneity is treated as the basis of solidarity and Shin notes tolerance is limited.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: State nationalism justified emergency rule, while ethnic nationalists opposed authoritarianism; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a nationalist position outside North Korea.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Shin notes citizenship by bloodline favors co-ethnics over immigrants.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Left nationalists opposed US troops while conservative state nationalists backed the alliance, so split.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not a Korean nationalist position; conscription is the mainstream form.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The ideology does not rank rural versus urban life; neutral.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Centrist minjok nationalists tried to prevent division in 1945-50 and the Sunshine Policy sought peaceful reunification; the minjok is one nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; nationalist historians were themselves scholars.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalists take pride in Korean culture but reject colonial hierarchy of civilizations; no firm view.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not part of nationalist doctrine; adherents split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: South Korea uses jus sanguinis, which reinforces attachment to overseas Koreans, and a 2005 birthright proposal was dropped under public opinion.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Shin notes ethnic nationalism limited cultural tolerance and liberalism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Shin's declaration lists economic exploitation and inequality as targets beyond foreign rule, though mainstream nationalism seldom says this.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not a nationalist doctrine.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: State nationalism justified authoritarian developmentalism while ethnic nationalism opposed it, so adherents split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is outside Korean nationalism.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The Dokdo dispute is treated as symbolic of sovereignty with no compromise (Roh Moo-hyun), indicating reluctance to cede claimed homeland.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterization of the USSR is not a nationalist question.

collective-defense.rationale: Conservative strands back the US alliance while left nationalists oppose it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Shin's declaration frames Japan's 1910 annexation as foreign rule to be ended, and Koreans treat colonial rule as illegitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state power is not an ethnic-nationalist concern.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Shin condemns privileged classes and servile thought; a divine ruler is rejected outside North Korea's leader cult.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structure is not a nationalist issue.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is outside Korean nationalism.

refugee-return.rationale: Divided-family issues exist, but no stated doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Shin's historiography blurs Korea-Manchuria boundaries, but mainstream nationalism makes no such state claim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Shin linked Koreans and Manchurians genealogically, yet nationalism's political aim is a Korean state.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Court-majority relations are not a nationalist doctrine.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive design is not a Korean nationalist topic.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Shin's declaration favors armed uprising but adherents are split on method.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The declaration names a privileged class among the obstacles to be abolished.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist historiography (Shin's Doksa Sillon and Joseon Sanggosa) placed the nation's own history at the center.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Shin rejected Japanese claims that Korea was insignificant as a colonial agenda, and anti-colonial nationalism denies the tutelage argument.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalist identity was built around history, Dangun and national symbols, and the flag represents the ethnic nation for many.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is outside Korean nationalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not a stated aim; Korean nationalism is anti-imperial.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not a nationalist aim given export-led development.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Democratic nationalists accept it, though rights vs collective tension exists.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ethnic nationalism opposed authoritarian regimes in the democracy movement.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The ideology offers no doctrine of elite duty; Shin criticizes privileged classes but not paternalism specifically.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: North Korea's Juche stresses self-reliance, but South Korean nationalism accepts foreign investment.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Shin's historiography claims lost northern lands but mainstream politics does not demand it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nationalists stress Korean uniqueness, yet sources give no view on Western institutions' fit.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The democracy movement opposed military rule.

single-official-language.rationale: Shin held that preserving Hangul and Hanja was part of identity; one national language is natural.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Concern for the nation's continuity favors it over immigration.

informal-organisation.rationale: Shin's anarchist organizing is atypical; mainstream nationalism is not defined by this.

religious-nation.rationale: The minjok is defined by descent and culture, not by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Shin condemned servility toward China and Japan, and Korean nationalism is marked by hostility toward great powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The unified-nation framing favors national sharing.

defeat-communism.rationale: State nationalism fused anti-communism with minjok under Rhee, while left minjok nationalism sought reconciliation with the North, so adherents split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Korean nationalism has no doctrine on religion; its minjok framing treats Dangun worship and Korean religious traditions as national heritage, so an illusion-fading view is not shared.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: No doctrine on capitalism; South Korean state nationalism credits state-led capitalist growth while the anti-imperialist left condemns it, so adherents split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Gender economics is outside the ideology; Shin Chaeho-era anarchists and the left might agree but state nationalists would not.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The division of Korea made both capitalism and communism contested; Shin Chaeho and the DPRK Juche claim a third path while most South Korean nationalists do not, so strands split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nationalist historiography roots Korea in Dangun and Gojoseon, and the movement presses the Dokdo claim on historical grounds.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Korean nationalism arose against Japanese colonial rule, and Shin's Declaration condemns foreign rule and exploitation of the people.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nationalism cuts across left and right in Korea, with left minjok and conservative state strands, so adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Shin's Declaration condemns exploitation, but the movement has no theory of alienation; adherents are split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Shin's Declaration endorses armed revolutionary resistance to foreign rule, and the state strands defend the nation by arms.

rich-first.rationale: Left minjok nationalists criticised unbalanced growth while conservative state nationalists defended it; adherents are split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Left nationalists favour autonomy and engagement while conservatives back the US alliance, so adherents are split.

online-participation.rationale: No stated position; adherents are not divided on it along nationalist lines.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Minjok nationalism defines the nation by common descent and blood, so full political membership, even local, is a contested extension; the multiethnic debate shows resistance.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Korean nationalism has a tradition of national-service and youth mobilisation, from the Hwarang myth to the Korea Youth Corps of the Rhee era, and conscription for all men.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-foreign-domination nationalism opposes foreign troops on Korean soil, a recurring demand of nationalist movements concerning US bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Korean nationalism demands Japanese acknowledgement of forced labour, comfort women and cultural erasure, but these are not framed as mass killings, so the fit with genocide recognition is partial.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Declaration of the Korean Revolution endorses revolutionary violence against Japanese rule, and the independence tradition honours armed resistance.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Shin Chaeho's historiography traces the minjok to Dangun and treats the Korean people as one unbroken line from antiquity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Korean nationalism honours independence martyrs, such as Yu Gwan-sun and An Jung-geun, and the national cemetery system; martyrdom of the nation is central.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mainstream Korean nationalism is secular and historical; the spiritual-war framing is not described in the sources read.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Korean nationalism favours reunification and a single national state for all Koreans rather than a diaspora centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: The independence movement put the state first: liberation and independence were prerequisites; Shin Chaeho's history aimed at building national consciousness for that struggle.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Reunification of the divided peninsula into a single Korean state is a central aim of minjok nationalism.

independent-unions.rationale: Not part of the ideology; the strands split between state-run and independent unions.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The minjok is an ethnic nation of shared blood, and the nationalism asks Koreans to organise around the interests of that group.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in shared blood, culture and history is the core of minjok nationalism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The minjok is defined by shared blood, language, culture and history, and the nation is held to be one across the DMZ and the diaspora.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Korean nationalism grew as resistance to colonial and great-power domination, and the division of Korea is widely blamed on outside powers.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation lies outside the ideology and adherents are split by left and right strands.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The ideology has no settled view; Shin's anarchist strand stressed equality while state nationalism leaned traditional.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Economic questions lie outside the ideology; left minjok nationalists back unions, while state nationalists favoured developmental control of labour.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mainstream Korean nationalism seeks to build and capture a sovereign state; Shin Chaeho's anarchist turn is treated as a variant, so only mild disagreement.

sacred-nation.rationale: Minjok nationalism treats the nation as a community of shared blood traced to Dangun that endures across generations, a near-sacred bond.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a concept of Korean nationalism; regional disparity (for example Honam) is discussed in politics but the ideology is about the whole nation, so neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Korean nationalism has no labour doctrine, and its left and right strands split on unions, so this is left neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Nationalism here is ethnic rather than religious and has no stated position on interpretations of religion; strands differ.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The democracy movement and the DPRK state strand give opposite answers, so adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: No doctrine on this; the South Korean state strand and the DPRK strand would differ.

race-social-construct.rationale: Minjok nationalism holds that the Korean nation is a unit of shared blood and descent, the opposite of treating racial categories as social constructs, as the multiethnic-society source describes.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The ideology has no stance on gender policy and its strands differ.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Mainstream South Korean nationalism is anti-DPRK, so defending a planned state is rejected; the North Korean Juche strand would differ.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Korean nationalism traces the minjok to Dangun and the sacred territory of the peninsula, and Shin Chaeho's historiography makes defending the ancestral land central.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The ideology has no drug policy; its democracy-movement strand and South Korea's legal order point against killing without trial, which is an inference.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The ethnic minjok framework treats Koreans abroad, including in China, Japan and Russia, as part of the nation, and state nationalism supports ties with the diaspora.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Korean nationalism has no doctrine on this; the left-leaning and state-nationalist strands split over it.

self-ownership.rationale: Shin Gi-Wook notes that the ethnic nationalism privileges collective over individual rights, so full individual self-ownership is mildly disfavoured.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Economic questions are outside the ideology and adherents are split by strand.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The ideology has no welfare doctrine; the left and right strands differ on universal versus targeted provision.

national-resource-control.rationale: Opposition to foreign domination is the ideology's core, and Shin Chaeho's declaration condemns foreign exploitation of the nation's wealth.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; adherents have no settled view.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Shin's declaration ties national liberation to ending exploitation and privilege, and ethnic nationalism is common on the anti-imperialist left.

missingStatements.text: A nation's identity should rest on shared descent from a founding ancestor.
missingStatements.rationale: Korean nationalism traces the minjok to Dangun, and Shin Chaeho's historiography proclaimed Koreans his descendants.

missingStatements.text: Governments should officially protest foreign textbooks and shrines that downplay their country's colonial-era wrongs.
missingStatements.rationale: Textbook disputes, Yasukuni visits and comfort-women issues are core grievances of South Korean nationalism.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to one dispute (foreign textbooks and shrines); the bank already covers national history, memory and accountability through broader statements.

notes: Left minjok nationalism (anti-imperialist, pro-engagement with the North) and conservative state nationalism (anti-communist, pro-US-alliance) split on alliance, security and economic questions. Many answers are low-confidence inferences because the ideology is mostly about nationhood, not policy.
